notes.summary: Independent full-page foundation: continuous printed-PC on finite complete rational page arrangements is page convexity plus common entire-page ambient supports; exact rational-spatial REAL-PA primal majorants. No proper-domain theorem.
notes.detailedSummary: Proves the inherited-carrier support criterion using rational perspective approximation and compact-product separation, and reconstructs finite convex/polyhedral foundations, whole-boundary conjugacy and rational primal graph carriers. A continuous convex target bounded relative to its actual admitted finite real-PA convex reference on one complete affine page admits global uniform above-majorants with actual recession and real unrounded heights. These foundations alone do not synchronize several overlaps.
notes.text:
Work is an unverified draft; compilation and finite execution do not certify it. The claims and proofs below are independent reconstructions. No S298/S306/S307 or unregistered draft result is imported.

Conventions. A rational spatial carrier is a finite globally embedded rational complex containing every closed face. Literal PA has integral tangent-lattice slopes and rational constants in rational affine coordinates. REAL-PA is its finite real scalar extension. Printed PCC means rational endpoints x_i in cells sigma_i incident to one center face tau, real nonnegative alpha_i summing to one, and center x=sum alpha_i x_i in tau; the center may be real. Continuity is a separate hypothesis.

Finite foundations. Every finite conic representation can be reduced to independent active columns: from a dependence sum b_i v_i=0 with some b_i>0, subtract t b_i from coefficients, t=min_{b_i>0}a_i/b_i. Coefficients stay nonnegative and one vanishes. Each remaining inverse column map bounds coefficients by a constant times the vector norm. There are finitely many subsets, proving closedness of the cone by subsequences. Affine dependence reduction also imposes sum b_i=0, leaving at most s+1 points in dimension s; the hull of compact K is a continuous image of K^{s+1} times a compact simplex, hence compact. For a cone defined by inequalities, remove their joint kernel as lineality. In a complement their sum is positive on nonzero feasible vectors. Its section at one is bounded, since normalization of an unbounded sequence would give a nonzero joint-kernel vector. A bounded polyhedron is a vertex hull: at a nonvertex move in both signs of an active-row kernel direction to new active constraints and induct on active rank. Vertices solve finite full-rank systems, rational for rational rows. Homogenizing Ax<=b as Au<=tb, t>=0 yields finite point/recession generation of every polyhedron; include both signs of a lineality basis. Conversely finite point hull plus cone is a finite polyhedron by eliminating representation variables: pair every lower and upper bound at each elimination step. This also proves rationality of rational projections. Compact hull plus finite cone is closed by a convergent compact-summand subsequence.

Convex foundations. A finite convex function on full affine space is locally Lipschitz: vertex values bound it above on a cube, reflection through the center bounds it below on a smaller cube, and extension of short segments inside the bounded cube bounds secants by oscillation divided by a fixed extension length. A point z outside a closed convex set has a nearest w by finite-dimensional compactness; variation gives (w-z).(c-z)>=||w-z||^2>0. Applying this separation to (x,F(x)-t) below a closed epigraph and letting t decrease to zero supplies a limiting unit supporting normal. Its inward vertical component is positive: zero would force its horizontal part to vanish because the domain is full. Division gives a touching affine minorant. Touching supports prove F=F**. Directional derivatives are finite continuous sublinear by secant monotonicity, the local Lipschitz bound, rescaling and midpoint inequalities. A support of this derivative at v has zero constant, by testing 0 and 2v. Its linear minorants are exactly the subgradients of F at x, form a compact nonempty convex set, and attain every directional derivative.

A finite lsc convex a on compact polytope D is continuous even at its boundary. At p choose a fixed positive radius below every inactive facet slack divided by the row norm. For q close to p in D, the point p+radius*(q-p)/||q-p|| stays feasible: active rows are homogeneous along that direction and inactive rows retain slack. Convexity bounds a(q) above by a(p)+||q-p||*(M-a(p))/radius, where M is the largest vertex value. Lsc gives the other limiting bound. For a extended by infinity off D, below-graph separation at (p,t), p in D, has strictly positive vertical component by testing the same spatial fiber (p,a(p)). The resulting affine minorants prove a=a** on D. Outside D spatial separation, scaled arbitrarily, gives infinite double transform. These arguments apply in relative affine hulls and at a singleton.

Printed-endpoint passage. A point of a rational polyhedron is approximated by rational feasible points in its minimal face: impose active rows as equalities, use a rational particular solution/kernel basis, approximate coefficients and retain inactive strict slacks. For PCC discard zero weights and use perspective variables t_i=alpha_i x_i. The conditions A_i t_i<=alpha_i b_i, alpha_i>=0, sum alpha_i=1, sum t_i in tau are rational linear constraints. Close feasible rational configurations have positive coefficients and rational endpoints and centers. Continuity therefore extends printed tests to real endpoints with the same incidences.

Whole-page criterion. For any finite arrangement of distinct complete rational affine pages, a continuous function is printed PC iff it is convex on each whole page and has one ambient form supporting every whole page containing y at every real y. A convex carrier cell lies in a page, since its relative interior cannot be covered by finitely many proper affine subspaces: the product of their nonzero affine equations is a nonzero polynomial and cannot vanish on an open set. Near y all carrier cells meeting a sufficiently small neighborhood contain y; its minimal face is a face of each such cell. Short symmetric endpoints on a page therefore give legal real midpoint PCCs. These prove whole-page convexity: subtract a segment chord to get q with zero endpoint values; if q is positive somewhere, q(t)+delta*t^2 has an interior maximum for small delta>0, contradicted by a short midpoint inequality, whose perturbed endpoint average exceeds that maximum by delta*s^2. This does not coarsen the inherited carrier or assume a distant PCC.

For necessity of the common form, let K_i be the compact page subdifferentials at y and S the closed image of restriction from the dual of the sum of incident page tangent spaces. If K=product K_i misses S, minimize ||pr_{S-perp}z||^2 on K. With a=pr_{S-perp}z0 nonzero, first variation gives a.z>=||a||^2 for all z in K. Represent -a by directions w_i; orthogonality means sum w_i=0, and the sum of directional derivatives is max_{z in K}sum z_i(w_i)<=-||a||^2. Short actual incident endpoints y+t w_i form an equal-weight real PCC with negative cost, impossible by the perspective passage. Hence K meets S and supplies one support on all entire incident pages. Conversely every endpoint cell lies in a page containing the center; sum these whole-page supports and cancel linear terms to prove all PCCs on all carriers.

Exact primal majorants on one full page. Let gamma be the actual convex finite REAL-PA reference with rational carrier and positive actual recession, and f continuous convex bounded relative to gamma. Full-dimensional affine pieces of gamma are global supports by secants, so gamma=max_j(a_j x+b_j), h=max_j a_j x and Delta=conv{a_j}. Gamma-h and f-h are bounded. Every direction is in the recession cone of some carrier cell by taking an unbounded subsequence on its ray; h equals that cell's linear part. Positive growth gives h(v)>0 for nonzero v. The actual conjugate phi=f* has domain exactly Delta: inside, p.x<=h(x) bounds it above and evaluation at zero bounds below; outside, a separating direction makes the supremum infinite. It is convex lsc and therefore continuous on the entire actual polytope, including irrational boundary points. Biconjugacy implies f(x+v)<=f(x)+h(v); bounded difference gives exact recession h. Rational generators of the reference's recession cones, lifted to (u,h(u)), together with (0,1), generate exactly epi h.

For tolerance delta, rational samples compute the same conjugate supremum by continuity of f. At each p in Delta pick a rational sample within delta/2; whole conjugate continuity gives a neighborhood with error below delta. Compactness selects finitely many samples S, including any prescribed finite rational contacts. Thus phi-delta<=max_{s in S}(p.s-f(s))<=phi on all Delta. Form E=conv{(s,f(s))}+epi h. This is closed, full projection, and contained in epi f by convexity and the recession inequality. Fibers have attained finite bottoms Q. Direct optimization gives Q*=max samples on Delta and infinity elsewhere. Biconjugacy reverses the bounds to f<=Q<=f+delta globally. The sample lifts give exact contacts. Compact hull plus exact recession cone has precisely that cone as recession, by dividing a forward sequence by its parameter.

Rationality despite REAL heights. A lower graph face of E consists of exactly the sampled point generators and recession generators with zero exposing slack; the vertical ray is excluded. Its spatial projection is their rational hull/cone. Projection is an affine isomorphism on a graph face. Subfaces remain lower exposed by a sufficiently small perturbation of a lower exposing functional, using the finite generator slacks. Common projected points have unique lower heights, so projected graph faces meet in common faces. They yield a finite rational carrier. Continuous affine tuples on it satisfy rational matching equations evaluated on rational affine bases of shared faces. Rational Gaussian elimination gives a rational basis of that kernel; clearing each basis tuple's finitely many slope/constant denominators makes literal PA basis functions. Their real span contains the actual tuple. This proves genuine REAL-PA, not an irrational-wall maximum shortcut.

These are full proofs for complete pages and finite-dimensional polyhedral data. They alone give neither several-overlap assembly nor a proper-cell extension theorem. Full expanded proofs are in P05.1-paper.tex Sections2–4 and argument.md. Rerun the own finite illustrations with `python exact_checks.py`; their finite success does not prove these continuum claims.

notes.summary: Prescribed entire PA trace extension on a dependent common-H group lifts EVERY trace subgradient simultaneously, with exact recession and arbitrary additional primal error. This stronger quantifier enables later several-overlap assembly.
notes.detailedSummary: Independently reconstructs compact joint/separate conjugate fibers including their whole boundaries. Lowering simultaneous minimizers gives full-page convex extensions of any convex rational-spatial REAL-PA trace g between f_H and f_H+a. Finite primal conversion preserves all trace generators and recession, produces f_i<=Q_i<=f_i+a+b, and retains a common ambient support lifting each chosen q in partial g(y). This is a one-group mechanism, not general multi-face feasibility.
notes.text:
Use n1's proved full-page criterion, finite hull/dual foundations and primal majorants. All hypotheses are essential: finitely many complete rational equal-dimensional affine pages Q_i have every pair intersection exactly one nonempty rational H; original continuous convex f_i agree on H, are bounded relative to the restrictions gamma_i of the same actual admitted reference, and possess a common ambient support on entire pages at every y in H. A singleton group is allowed. Translate a rational point of H to zero. Let L_i be the page tangent spaces and E=sum L_i; r_i:E*->L_i*, T:E*->H*, U_i:L_i*->H* are restrictions. Write Delta_i for the actual gamma_i gradient polytopes, phi_i=f_i*, h_i for actual recession. The trace reference is actual convex rational-spatial REAL-PA positive-growth; its recession is h_H=h_i|H and its gradient polytope is Delta_H. For H a point use Delta_H={0}.

Joint fibers. Put D={p:r_i p in Delta_i for all i}, phi(p)=max_i phi_i(r_i p), G=phi*. D has finite real inequalities and is compact: a normalized unbounded sequence would have unit limit vanishing on every L_i, hence on E. A common support p_y gives simultaneous Fenchel equalities phi_i(r_i p_y)=p_y(y)-f_H(y), so D is nonempty. Whole continuity of phi_i makes phi continuous on D. Since phi>=phi_i composed with restriction, G|L_i<=f_i; the Fenchel equalities give G|H=f_H.

Define k(q)=min_{Tp=q,p in D}phi(p). Compact fibers attain minima. Mixing minimizers proves convexity; a subsequence of minimizing p values for convergent q gives lsc, including its infinity extension because T(D) is closed. It is finite on compact polytope T(D), so n1 proves whole boundary continuity and biconjugacy. Grouping the transform by fibers gives k*=G|H=f_H. Hence k=f_H*, and its domain is exactly Delta_H. Repeat with the separate restriction U_i and phi_i: its fiber minimum has conjugate f_i|H=f_H, hence equals the same k with the same full domain. Therefore each phi_i(r_i p)>=k(Tp). At a joint minimizer their maximum equals k(q), forcing equality for EVERY page. M={p in D:phi(p)=k(Tp)} is compact by continuity and maps onto every q in Delta_H, including boundary fibers. Dependence among page directions causes no loss of simultaneous minimizers.

Prescribe a finite convex rational-spatial REAL-PA trace g on all H with f_H<=g<=f_H+a, a>=0. It has unchanged actual trace recession by bounded difference. Let c=g*. N1 gives its entire domain Delta_H, whole continuity, and k-a<=c<=k. For each page form K_i=conv(graph phi_i union {(r_i p,c(Tp)):p in M})+nonnegative vertical ray. The source sets are compact, their hull is compact by n1, and adding the vertical ray is closed. Projection is all Delta_i. Source heights are bounded, so fibers have finite attained bottoms psi_i, finite convex lsc and whole continuous.

At an added source, simultaneous minimization gives phi_i(r_i p)=k(Tp), so its lowered height is at least phi_i-a. All original sources obey the same bound. Convexity gives phi_i-a<=psi_i<=phi_i. Every original source also has height at least k(U_i z)>=c(U_i z); added sources have equality with c. Consequently psi_i>=c composed with U_i. For any q select ONE joint p in M over it. Added sources show psi_i(r_i p)=c(q) simultaneously, and the minimum of psi_i over each q-fiber is exactly c(q). Set F_i=psi_i*. They are finite continuous convex on whole pages, with f_i<=F_i<=f_i+a, exact recession h_i, and F_i|H=c*=g.

Universal support lift. Fix ANY y in H and ANY q in partial g(y). Fenchel equality gives g(y)=q(y)-c(q) and q in Delta_H. Choose one joint p in M over q. For every page and every x, F_i(x)>=(r_i p)(x)-psi_i(r_i p)=g(y)+p(x-y). Thus the prescribed q, not merely some unrelated trace support, lifts to ONE ambient form supporting every whole page. This quantifier is the key addition required by n3.

Finite PA conversion without changing a whole trace. Refine the rational carrier of g by rational coordinate orthants if needed to make cells pointed. Finite rational point/ray generation on each cell and affine graph heights give epi g=conv{(v,g(v)):v in V}+epi h_H for a finite rational point list V. Inclusion in epi g follows from convexity and recession stability; reverse inclusion uses the generating cell containing each point, whose actual ray heights equal h_H. For H a point take one graph lift and the vertical ray. Apply n1's full-page primal majorant theorem to each F_i with additional tolerance b>0, appending EVERY v in V. The resulting Q_i satisfy F_i<=Q_i<=F_i+b, are genuine finite rational-spatial REAL-PA, and have exact h_i recession. Their primal epigraphs contain every trace lift and epi h_H. The entire trace epigraph identity gives Q_i|H<=g; the bound Q_i>=F_i gives equality. Hence f_i<=Q_i<=f_i+a+b globally. Every lifted common support below F_i remains below Q_i and still touches at every trace point. This retains a lift for EVERY q in partial g(y).

No measure is assigned to F_i or dual intermediates. All generators, closedness, finite attained fibers, irrational dual boundaries, actual real heights and genuine scalar matching are justified by n1. This independently proved one-group mechanism is not imported from S298 and is not claimed as the new general classification. Expanded proof: P05.1-paper.tex Section5 and argument.md. No supplied programs were run.

notes.summary: New finite all-face REAL-PA approximation for finitely many freely attached dependent page groups, allowing SEVERAL distinct positive-dimensional overlaps. All real face points and entire incident original cells are controlled; general complexes remain open.
notes.detailedSummary: A geometric affine-span intersection condition, independent of the target or carrier feasibility, permits finite assembly from a parent approximation. Every earlier whole trace stays fixed. The universal support lift of n2 matches the old support restriction at all multiple intersections; elementary linear amalgamation gives one common ambient form. A finite eps/(r+1) budget proves arbitrary global error and existence of a finite rational carrier. Common dyadic shifts produce strict global decreasing approximation with actual recession and one relative bound. Positive actual real weights balance separately on complete pages.
notes.text:
The new scope is the following geometric class, not arbitrary singular complexes. In one lattice real space start with a complete rational affine d-page Q0, d>=1. At step j=1,...,r attach finitely many distinct complete rational d-pages Q_{j,a}, all containing one nonempty rational affine H_j of dimension<d and pairwise intersecting exactly in H_j. H_j lies in one earlier parent page. Let A_{j-1}=aff X_{j-1} and E_j=aff union_a Q_{j,a}; require E_j intersect A_{j-1}=H_j. For a singleton new group the pairwise clause is vacuous. This rational geometric criterion is decidable by affine linear algebra and does not assume any PA band system feasible. H_j may differ from earlier attachments and meet them along lower-dimensional subspaces. Directions within any group may be dependent.

Theorem. For every actual continuous rational-spatial REAL-PA PC reference gamma positive at infinity, every continuous printed-PC target f with ||f-gamma||<=C, and eps>0, there is genuine finite rational-spatial REAL-PA PC P with f<=P<=f+eps globally, exact actual page recession, and a common ambient affine support at EVERY real point on EVERY ENTIRE incident complete page. In particular the same support works on ENTIRE incident closed cells of any fixed finite rational original carrier, including its proper cells and all faces. Complete-page support, rather than complete original carrier cells, is the crucial hypothesis. The theorem gives existence of a finite carrier, not only a fixed-carrier feasibility test.

Proof. N1 gives original full-page convexity and common whole-page supports. Put t=eps/(r+1). Its primal theorem supplies a root P0 with error<=t and exact recession. Inductively maintain continuity, convexity on every whole page, genuine finite rational-spatial REAL-PA, exact recession, common entire-page supports at all points and error<=jt on X_{j-1}. Leave all earlier values untouched. The parent approximation restricts to a finite convex REAL-PA trace g_j on all H_j with f_H<=g_j<=f_H+jt. Bounded difference gives its exact actual trace recession. The original target restricted to the new group meets n2's hypotheses, including simultaneous whole-page support. Apply n2 with a=jt, b=t, obtaining new page Q functions with error<=(j+1)t, exact g_j trace and exact actual recession.

At any real y in H_j, let p_old support all incident earlier entire pages; extend it linearly to the earlier affine span if needed. Its restriction q to T H_j supports the entire parent trace, so q is in partial g_j(y). N2 lifts THIS q to p_new supporting all new entire pages. With origin at y, the tangent intersection of A_{j-1} and E_j is exactly T H_j. Define p(u+v)=p_old(u)+p_new(v); differences of decompositions lie in that intersection and the forms agree there. This gives one common ambient support on all incident pages. This remains valid where H_j meets earlier H_l: the parent is incident, and p_old already supports every incident old page. No smaller face is declared exposed in an incident-union hull. Away from H_j no old/new page meets, and away from H_j inside the new group only one page is present. Thus all other supports are retained or supplied by page convexity. Common whole traces give continuity by finite closed-page gluing. N1's criterion gives all PCCs on all carriers. The induction is finite and final error<=(r+1)t=eps.

Finite global rational carrier. Extend every rational wall equation of each page carrier, all equations needed to cut page intersections into faces, and all fixed original-carrier walls to rational ambient affine equations. A single finite ambient hyperplane arrangement restricted to all pages refines their carriers and the original carrier; cut cells meet in common faces. It does not compare unrelated real coefficients. Matching real tuples satisfy a rational kernel system and hence belong to the finite real scalar extension by n1. Supports, values and recession remain unchanged. Each original incident closed cell lies in a page containing its face point, so the entire-page support proves the promised entire original-cell condition.

For decreasing uniform approximation choose unshifted Q_n with 0<=Q_n-f<=eta_n=2^{-n}, n>=1, and set P_n=Q_n+4eta_n on every page. Then 4eta_n<=P_n-f<=5eta_n and P_n-P_{n+1}>=4eta_n-5eta_{n+1}=3eta_n/2>0. All common traces/supports remain, recession is unchanged, uniform convergence is global, and ||P_n-gamma||<=C+5/2. The shifts lose unshifted sample contacts.

Actual positive real all-face balance. Assign arbitrary specified positive constant c_i to each complete page. On a common rational carrier, every page facet has two adjacent top cells with equal c_i and opposite saturated primitive inward quotient classes. They cancel page by page, including shared facets. Sum the page contributions to verify every original balancing equation with real weights and no omitted boundary. The formal BMPS weight class is rational; this actual-real verification is independent of it.

PA positivity also has a direct proof in every cycle dimension. For a nonnegative balanced local k-cycle c and a (k-1)-face rho, the actual primitive formula is sum_{sigma>rho} c(sigma)P_sigma(n_{sigma/rho}) minus P_rho(sum c(sigma)n_{sigma/rho}). At a relative interior point subtract the common ambient support p, whose derivative equals P_rho in both tangent signs. Balancing cancels p's contribution and every residual inward slope is nonnegative. Tangential lift changes cancel. Thus no source equivalence, gcd, unit-normal sign replacement or operator is required.

This finite one-way assembly preserves several distinct overlaps simultaneously and does not rerun independent individual-face corrections. Its failure boundary is precise: if span intersection is larger than H_j, old/new forms need to agree on more directions than n2 controls; the amalgamation has no conclusion. General proper-support cells, cyclic/non-free arrangements and necessity/classification remain unresolved. Complete expanded paper: P05.1-paper.tex, 16-page P05.1-paper.pdf, argument.md; coverage in proof-coverage.md. Rerun `python exact_checks.py` and the no-shell TeX commands recorded in execution-record.md.

notes.summary: Actual unrestricted ALL-C_b envelopes on the new several-overlap class enter the proved REAL-PA domain; seven-plane dependent two-line-overlap example and all products, including nonseparable targets/obstacles.
notes.detailedSummary: Checks the positive-real embedded all-face balance of n3, then uses qualified R230 solely for actual endpoint continuity and bounded-relative PC. N3 supplies PA approximation afterward. An explicit seven-plane arrangement in R^6 has two different parent overlap lines and dependent directions in each group, hence is outside one-common-H geometry. Its unchanged integral reference has positive recession and a non-PA target with a nonzero mixed derivative; all C_b obstacles and arbitrary products are covered, without an operator/contact conclusion.
notes.text:
Actual envelope. On n3's finite positive-real balanced globally embedded rational arrangement, retain the admitted actual continuous PC real-PA positive-growth gamma. For any u in C_b(X), define exactly P_gamma(u)(x)=sup{q(x):q finite printed-PC, q<=gamma+u, q<=gamma+C_q globally for some real C_q}. Competitors may be discontinuous and have only upper growth control; none is replaced by a PA/sampled competitor class. The complete qualified grant R230 supplies continuity, printed PC, identification with the continuous-competitor envelope and gamma+inf u<=P<=gamma+u<=gamma+sup u. Its hypotheses hold by n3's all-face real balance and the actual continuous reference/obstacle. Hence ||P-gamma||<=||u|| and n3 applies to this actual endpoint, giving genuine global decreasing REAL-PA PC approximation with actual recession. R230 alone does not prove PA density. The optional upper-only versus bounded-relative competitor identification follows directly by replacing q with max(q,gamma-||u||); this is a PC comparison, not an irrational PA max claim. No MA or contact measure is assigned here.

New geometry. In R^6 with standard lattice use Q0=span(e1,e2); v1=e3,v2=e4,v3=-e3-e4; w1=e5,w2=e6,w3=-e5-e6. First attach the three span(e1,v_i) along H1=R e1; then the three span(e2,w_i) along H2=R e2. Equating coordinates proves each group's pair intersection is its line, first group span meets Q0 exactly in H1, and second group span meets the previous span span(e1,e2,e3,e4) exactly in H2. Cross-group pages meet at 0. The v_i and w_i each sum to zero and are dependent. The seven-plane union therefore meets n3's free geometric condition and has TWO different actual unbounded positive-dimensional overlaps. Every pair intersection is not one H, so it is outside the supplied exact S298 common-H geometry.

The actual reference gamma=|x1+x2|+|x1-x2|+sum_{k=3}^6|xk| is ambient convex, literal integral PA on rational walls, and positive in every nonzero recession direction because the six linear forms have zero joint kernel. Assign any positive real page weights; n3 proves balancing. A continuous non-PA target is f=phi(x1+x2)+phi(x1-x2)+sum_{k=3}^6 phi(xk), phi(t)=sqrt(1+t^2)-1. Since phi''=(1+t^2)^(-3/2)>0 it is ambient convex and satisfies all printed PCCs. The inequalities |t|<=sqrt(1+t^2)<=|t|+1 prove -6<=f-gamma<=0 globally. On Q0 at (1/2,1/2), the mixed derivative is 1/(2sqrt2)-1, nonzero, so f is not a sum of separate root-coordinate functions. N3 regularizes it, but the theorem's universal scope is ALL continuous relative-PC targets and, through R230, ALL C_b actual envelopes, not merely this ambient-convex example.

Products with R^k preserve all span/intersection identities by taking their products, and each H becomes H times R^k. Add sum|z_l| to the actual reference. Positive recession is retained. For every k>=0 the same theorem covers all bounded continuous obstacles, including obstacles depending jointly on old and product coordinates. Thus the application has dimension d=2+k and arbitrary nonseparable obstacle domains within this geometric class. It does not extend the theorem to arbitrary non-free complexes.

Application and proof are in P05.1-paper.tex Sections7–8 and argument.md. All sample heights in the actual construction are real and unrounded; literal regularity is not inferred merely because this illustrative gamma is literal.
